approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current objective’s scored observations. It keeps every accepted observation for learning and a greedy population of 64 for breeding, draws parents from score quantiles, and builds fresh pools through connected-fragment crossover and bounded atom, bond and ring mutations with continuation and rejection recovery. Stable canonical isomeric admission rejects duplicates and source-relative introductions of specified sulfur environments. An accepted-only Gaussian process on chirality-aware local environment counts scores each fresh pool; correlated sampled residuals around its raw predicted means choose the announced batch through sequential masks and stable ties. Accepted scores then update both the archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add one fixed molecular-pretrained-feature location recipe. A frozen chemical language encoder represents each complete nonisomeric molecular view, and a second Gaussian process learns its relationship to the current objective’s accepted scores. Its raw mean supplies half the allocation location, with the original count predictor supplying half and the original correlated residual still providing exploration. Earlier siblings tried hand-designed kernel changes, likelihood-selected descriptor mixtures and a synthetic-pretrained tabular response model. This recipe instead tests unlabeled molecular pretraining through a separate fixed feature GP and fixed mean blend. The claim is that complementary molecular context can improve prospective ordering and absolute productive progress; the complete endpoint comparison will decide whether that helps search.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is weak, inconsistently productive allocation of fresh graph offspring, rather than a demonstrated defect of one covariance. I opened all three actual n-1744a1494180 summary.json/run.log pairs and scanned all fifteen full optimizer logs. The complete mean is 0.59645311428869 with population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. Every task completed at 300 calls, batch ten, with zero external invalid or duplicate proposals. Only 648/4350 accepted offspring strictly beat their best ORIGINAL scored generating parent; their mean score is 0.372049560842182 against mean best-parent score 0.4553040448335956, signed margin -0.08325448399141373. There are 255 sequential incumbent advances with total magnitude 5.819415048695714. The Parent learns and advances, but most accepted offspring lose absolute utility relative to their source. Its sulfur gate adds only +0.0007834645552323346 versus its own Parent, with mixed seed signs. The retained count view encodes local environment multiplicities; molecular contextual information is a candidate explanation to test, not an established mediator. Contrary evidence is binding: n-14a52e3f8725 improves same-label ordering and MSE while losing 0.05826897931006499 endpoint mean; n-5cc22bb8f56b improves prediction but loses about 0.0131 with composition-associated size/uncertainty drift; n-52bd6c308406 loses same-label ordering and endpoint mean 0.077227 on normalized count directions. n-e75f0f495f9b adds atom-pair information and modest prediction gains yet loses 0.033408 on its different ungated Parent. n-3062f0c87203 worsens ordering under its fixed TabPFN recipe; its original Anchor comparison is cross-lock and unpaired. The exact inherited-lock active-location removal n-fe734eb5c1df gains 0.05167897370782667 against that treatment, with fourteen endpoint gains and one loss, establishing an adverse conditional TabPFN-location contribution, not rejection of all frozen chemical representations. These observations motivate preserving the useful original residual while testing one fixed new location recipe. Parent late deco_hop seed-0 endpoint 0.8561477222467935 remains in the primary panel; repeated ancestral trajectories are dependent realizations.

literature_review.conclusion: This is a new searched review dated2026-10-04, additionally grounded in the actual .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-search-policy/external-method-review.md. I independently searched the listed queries, read the primary manuscript and pinned official source, and fetched/hashes-checked small official files into r32-slot0-plan. Its official-source-receipts.json records actual redirected official resolve-cache URLs and bytes; official source/vocabulary hashes match the primary review. Adopt exactly the pinned unlabeled molecular encoder through the fixed angular feature GP/equal raw location blend while preserving original residuals. Published predictive transfer is sufficient motivation to test complementary context, not evidence of successful productive exploration or endpoint transfer. Earlier same-label prediction gains with endpoint losses demand separate real-feedback, absolute progress and complete matched endpoint tests. ChemBERTa alternatives stay deferred for the primary review’s unresolved checkpoint-license provenance; no alternative checkpoint or blend sweep is registered. Exact-lock offline loader/parity/resource checks remain APPLY construction obligations, not completed checks or experimental evidence.

finding_summary.headline: MoLFormer changed most choices, but weakened ranking and lost 0.06811 in the complete matched panel
finding_summary.insights: This fixed recipe was fully exposed, so its loss cannot be attributed to a missing checkpoint, a silent count-only substitute, an incomplete panel or an untested allocation change. Both registered ranking aggregates decline, and the decline is larger among changed choices. Better local-win counts and more productive new cores did not produce stronger absolute progress: breeding-source scores were lower, positive improvement magnitudes shrank, and gains arrived later. The early-budget cumulative gain was 1.953179 versus 3.602660 for the Parent; some middle-budget recovery did not restore the endpoints. The chemistry assessment shows moderate diversity and some ordinary aromatic amides and diaryl amines, alongside larger linked heterocycles, reactive attachments and dense cages. The larger deco-hop family did not recover the Parent’s compact late high-label arrangement, and fewer N-halogen structures in the sitagliptin family still accompanied a large endpoint loss. Extra cores or fewer suspect local motifs therefore do not establish useful independent chemical alternatives or chemical repair. Those associations do not identify why the predictor or endpoint changed. The result supports negative contribution of this one fixed encoder-view, pooling, angular-GP and equal-blend combination on the inherited sulfur-gated count search. It does not isolate the encoder, pooling, feature kernel, mixing coefficient or location/residual interaction, and it does not reject molecular pretraining generally. Unselected reference alternatives have no counterfactual labels or continuations, so ranking-to-score mediation remains open. Natural inference included 107 complete pool views above the 202-token pretraining cutoff, including one accepted 220-token view; that establishes full-view exposure, not benefit on long molecules. Unsupported-row and failure routing passed construction checks but had no natural exposure. The small raw pooling tolerance exception is retained, while the normalized GP embeddings passed the registered checks. This completes the fixed recipe’s exposed test and supplies evidence for review without a result-driven rescue sweep.
finding_summary.results: The frozen molecular encoder and equal raw-mean blend executed in all 15 task/seed sessions. Every one of the 69,600 fresh-pool rows and 4,350 accepted offspring was supported; there were no unsupported-row or numerical batch fallbacks. The location changed 2,368 of 4,350 accepted choices under the same saved count residuals and actual masks. Of those changed choices, 2,282 reached both learners at the next fit and 86 were in the terminal batch. On the same prospective accepted labels, active pair-order accuracy fell from 0.670954 for the original count mean to 0.669109, and mean within-batch Spearman fell from 0.436926 to 0.428857. The auxiliary mean alone was weaker at 0.618377 and 0.311806. Active MSE rose from 0.006501 to 0.006680. Compared with the code Parent, mean accepted-offspring score fell from 0.372050 to 0.334941. Strict best-parent wins increased from 648 to 700, but their summed positive margins fell from 17.251535 to 12.579418, and summed sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819415 to 4.797752. The complete matched three-seed macro mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.528342, a delta of -0.068111 against the registered +0.002 goal. All three seed macros fell (-0.094788, -0.027975 and -0.081569), and 10 of the 15 task/seed endpoints fell. Mean endpoint changes were -0.010466 on zaleplon, -0.096673 on deco hop, -0.001594 on docking, +0.003991 on median, and -0.235812 on sitagliptin. Macro dispersion decreased from 0.033970 to 0.019708. This is confirmed allocation activation with failed ordering, productive-progress and performance predictions.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and diaryl amines coexist with oversized heterocycles, reactive appendages and densely bridged rings
molecular.overall_character: Node n-61c472c961cc produces recognizable compact aromatic amides, diaryl aliphatic amines, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aromatic/amide medium-ring systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Different seeds supply distinct families; within a seed the high-label molecules often remain close substitution or ring-connectivity variants. This is moderate chemical diversity, not global scaffold collapse. All 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories were read in full. Every path exists and has 300 chronologically ordered records, including ten initials and 290 accepted optimizer observations; the digest covers 900 records and 870 optimizer observations per objective. No task, path or paired seed comparison is absent. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with matched Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 and no profile mismatch. Parent chemistry and scores below come from those published trajectories, reached through the request's focus.artifacts and evidence_index; the Parent molecular report was also read. The digest's final_molecules are only the last seed-2 proposals and are not the seed endpoints. Ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.969 to 0.9966 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9494 to 0.9908. These are molecule-level text incidences, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Explicit charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout; neutral notation nevertheless includes potentially basic amines. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 perception of recorded structures finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2115 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, with none explicitly specified, versus 2455 of 4350 Parent observations. Size and motif counts are structure readings documented, with path hashes and all recorded labels, in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-slot0-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_receipt.json; they are not new oracle, synthetic-accessibility, stability or pharmacology scores. The more ordinary amide and amine examples prevent a uniformly implausible judgement, while acid chlorides, direct N/O-halogen bonds, nitroso/nitrite groups and difficult connected-ring geometry keep overall plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Chemistry associations do not decide activation, mediation, component contribution or algorithm eligibility. The comparison concerns the single joint fixed encoder-view/pooling/angular-GP/location-blend recipe under the inherited graph, sulfur-admission and feedback conditions; none of those components is isolated here.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted optimizer molecules have a median of 24 heavy atoms and span 1 to 48. The leading families have three perceived aromatic rings and 23-25 heavy atoms. Seed 1 gives an ethyl/methoxy/fluoro azaindole-like fused heterocycle bearing an N-methyl anilide and aryl chlorine or fluorine. That local chemistry is comparatively conventional. Seed 0 instead retains an N-amino aryl amide on an indole-like core; seed 2 uses an indole/pyridyl ketone with a terminal imine. Ordinary aromatic carbonyl chemistry coexists with N-halogen amides, O-halogen attachments, thiocarbonyls and overgrown coupled heterocycles. The Parent likewise reaches compact fused aromatic carbonyl families; its seed-1 leader retains N-F and an N-hydroxy amide. The Child is not missing rings or aromatic carbonyl groups, and its most ordinary seed-1 leader does not establish a general synthetic improvement.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 144 of 870 Child optimizer observations and direct O-halogen bonds in 85; these are separate local reactivity concerns, not evidence that every aryl halide or N-hydroxy amide is problematic.

The N-amino amide and terminal imine leaders require environment-specific stability and synthesis assessment. Very large joined aromatic systems lose useful context despite retaining familiar substructures.
missing_features: Conventional substitutions preserving the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl relationship are available in seed 1 but are not consistently supplied across the other leading families: N-amino amides, terminal imines and N-halogen alternatives remain prominent.
Independent plausible realizations at the higher Parent labels remain unestablished. The record does not support a blanket need for more rings, sulfur, halogens or any exact unseen target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide has label 0.3051048083696145. The Child seed-1 N-methyl azaaryl anilide reaches 0.46092619585962435. A matched fluoro-anilide without the extra fused-ring fluorine has label 0.4531365599537262; replacing N-methyl by N-H in the otherwise fluorinated series gives 0.2928991775375014. Thus the observed gradient recognizes a particular compact substitution/carbonyl arrangement, not simply aromatic mass or halogen count. Chlorine/fluorine changes on the anilide can tie, while an adjacent diketone/N-chloroamide variant still scores 0.4524187090179798. A doubled 48-heavy-atom indole system scores 4.075774319235988e-14 and methane scores 0.0. The observed Child seed-best labels in order 0, 1, 2 are 0.4425635194548914, 0.46092619585962435 and 0.43554057891621306; published Parent labels are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. These small chemical differences do not identify a unique absent target pharmacophore or an isolated encoder effect.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest output family: median 43 heavy atoms, range 1 to 120, versus Parent median 31. Seed 1's 38-heavy-atom leader has five perceived rings, four aromatic: linked azaaryl regions, a fused oxygen/carbonyl heterocycle, a cyclic thioether, methoxy/fluoroalkoxy groups and fluorinated carbon substituents. Seed 0's 47-heavy-atom leader joins nitrogen-rich dione/azole regions into medium and large cycles and bears carbamoyl-chloride functionality; its ring perception includes eight- and ten-membered cycles. Seed 2 favors smaller azaaryl/fused dione arrangements with carbon-bound nitroso groups, while late alternatives carry aryl nitrite groups. Some heterocycles are recognizable, but extensive annulation, reactive appendages and giant concatenations make the full output synthetically questionable. The Parent seed-0 late leader is a more compact linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione arrangement, though it too has O-F and unusual peripheral chemistry.
liabilities: Acyl-halogen connectivity occurs in 56 of 870 Child optimizer observations versus three Parent observations. It includes N-bound carbonyl chloride appendages and should not be conflated with ordinary aryl chlorine.

The Child has 178 N=O-containing observations, including 117 O-N=O nitrite matches; these overlapping counts distinguish carbon-bound nitroso groups from nitrite attachments rather than counting them as independent liabilities.
Large heterocyclic annulations and molecules with up to 120 heavy atoms raise conformational and synthesis questions. More aromatic strings do not certify accessible geometry.
missing_features: The compact linked heterocyclic arrangement associated with the Parent's late high label is not reproduced at a comparable label in the Child seed-0 stream; the Child instead emphasizes a much larger annulated dione/azole family.

Stable peripheral alternatives preserving favorable ring relationships are not established for the acid-chloride and nitroso/nitrite series. Tied fluorinated substituents do not identify a uniquely required group, and the higher Parent leader itself is not a chemically validated answer.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent for the fluoroalkoxy centre of the seed-1 leader; the record supplies no stereochemical score comparison.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic fused dione has label 0.548381482770623, whereas isolated fluorine and other tiny fragments sit at 0.5. Seed 1 reaches 0.6217782710568505 in its linked azaaryl/thioether family; replacing one fluoromethyl with difluoromethyl yields the same label. A 120-heavy-atom aromatic concatenation scores 0.6085707720588236, so very large aromatic coverage is not sufficient for the higher label. The Child seed-best labels are 0.6018637711982986, 0.6217782710568505 and 0.6071571973499297. Published Parent labels are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. In particular, the Parent seed-0 compact carbonyl/thione arrangement first attains its highest label at evaluation 281; the Child's large acid-chloride-bearing family does not show that chemical solution. This is an observed structural association, not a claim that a particular reactive substituent, compactness or ring count caused the difference.

per_task.generated_character: The three Child leaders contain 25-31 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings connected through an aliphatic amine region. Seed 0 gives a tertiary N-methyl diaryl chain with terminal alkyne, phenol, methoxy, aryl chlorine and a benzylic fluorine. Seed 1 gives a more conventional tertiary diaryl amine with propyl, methoxy, phenol and aryl bromine substituents. A high-label seed-0 ring-closed tertiary amine also exists, so cyclic basic centres are not absent. Seed 2 instead keeps a thioether/diaryl chain with unsaturation and chloro-substituted aminal/amine environments. Median Child size is 32 heavy atoms, versus Parent 29. The Parent high-label chemistry likewise combines aryl regions with free cyclic amines, including a seven-membered diaza/aminal ring. The Child seed-0 and seed-1 leaders have comparatively plausible local functional groups; their unassigned stereochemistry and the seed-2 reactive chain limit stronger conclusions.
liabilities: Seed-2 high-label molecules carry chlorinated aminal/alpha-amino carbon environments and substantial unsaturation; their hydrolytic and synthetic behavior is untested.

The digest cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0782, and the structure audit finds 68 carbon-allene-containing observations among 870. The late quoted allene is a distinct concern from ordinary isolated alkenes.
Halogen-string incidence is 0.9851. Many are conventional aryl halides, but halogen-rich mass, reactive attachment context and unspecified stereochemistry require separate assessments.
missing_features: Consistently stable local realizations of the aryl/amine relationship are missing from the seed-2 leading chain and some neighboring aminal variants, even though the other seeds demonstrate conventional alternatives.

Configuration at benzylic/fluorinated or substituted aminal centres is not specified. Neutral SMILES does not establish missing protonation, and these records do not determine a unique required charge state.
Conformationally credible alternatives remain a conditional gap, not a universal lack of cyclic amines: both Child and Parent already show high-label ring-closed examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: High labels associate with an intact aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement. The Child seed-0 diaryl tertiary amine scores 0.9964979655318211 and a cyclized relative scores 0.9882038452486718; the seed-1 comparatively ordinary tertiary amine scores 0.9895628567317698. In contrast, a simple propyl aryl sulfoxide scores 0.00018602945783559319 and the N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197. These differences do not isolate basicity, but show that aryl halogen or heteroatom presence alone is insufficient. A 108-heavy-atom joined initial-like molecule scores 0.028858376881499982. Seed 2's haloaminal/diaryl leader still scores 0.9822087248603178, whereas a late allene-containing variant scores 0.8981108784697664: problematic chemistry can receive high labels. Child seed-best labels are 0.9964979655318211, 0.9895628567317698 and 0.9822087248603178, versus Parent 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. No shortage of basic nitrogen or two-ring aryl coverage explains these small, differently signed comparisons.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted output has median 31 heavy atoms, matching the Parent, and spans 2 to 64. The Child leaders have 32 heavy atoms and four or five perceived rings. Seed 0 combines pyrrole/azole and phenyl-ethoxy regions with a tertiary amine and N-methyl amide in connected medium rings; a nearby high-label version has an eleven-membered amide/amine/ether ring. Seed 1 retains propylquinoline connected through O-N/N-N chemistry to a nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl system. Seed 2 has quinoline/aryloxy and partially unsaturated connected nitrogen/dicarbonyl rings. The Parent leaders likewise combine quinoline or other aromatic regions with cyclic nitrogen and carbonyl groups, rather than lacking those functions. Recognizable amide, ether and amine chemistry is present, but repeated cross-links, N-N/O-N connections and medium-ring geometry make apparent synthesis more demanding than the familiar fragments alone suggest.
liabilities: Connected medium rings and constrained unsaturation require geometric assessment beyond valence and aromatic notation; the eleven-membered example is not intrinsically impossible.
O-N and N-N connections in leading families must be distinguished by their complete environment rather than treated as interchangeable with ordinary carbon-linked amines.
The larger joined relative demonstrates loss of useful context despite retention of recognizable aromatic and amide substructures.
missing_features: Simpler, geometrically credible realizations retaining the favorable aromatic/amine/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently established at the leading labels; more cross-linked graphs are available but are not validated conformers or syntheses.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of substituted connected-ring variants remains unresolved. The record does not support a shortage of nitrogen, carbonyl groups or rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione has label 0.1678386594791329, while methanol and methylamine proposals score 0.008773280079294957. An eleven-membered amide/amine/ether relative in seed 0 scores 0.23567625760869773 and its more cross-linked leader scores 0.2376130302352129; useful growth or reconnection is therefore possible. Yet attaching another large related region produces a 56-heavy-atom molecule with label 0.18428853505018536. The observed gradient favors particular aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships rather than general ring abundance or size. Child seed-best labels are 0.2376130302352129, 0.22155892906015615 and 0.22099501762303972; published Parent labels are 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. Seed 2 reaches a different cross-linked family from the Parent's less cross-linked quinoline/dicarbonyl nitrogen rings. These records do not establish an exact missing target motif or a consistent chemical effect of greater connectivity.

per_task.generated_character: Median size is 28 heavy atoms versus Parent 27, with Child optimizer output spanning 1 to 51. Seed 0's 30-heavy-atom leader combines a difluorophenyl methyl ester with a nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino region, direct N-F substitution and a fused/bridged fluorinated cyclopropane arrangement bearing a thiol. Seed 1's 30-heavy-atom leader adds an N-methyl formamide, a fluorinated cyclopentadiene-like region and a fused nitrogen/oxygen dione system with N-F. Seed 2's 26-heavy-atom leader is a dense phenolic cage with thioester and cyclic urea/carbonyl functionality; eight cycles are perceived, with multiple possible tetrahedral centres. The Parent's higher-label families are generally less cross-linked compact fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems, but they also carry N-F or difficult small-ring geometry. Rich ring counts and fluorination therefore coexist with substantial synthetic and geometric uncertainty in both nodes.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen connectivity remains in 298 of 870 Child optimizer observations, versus 425 Parent observations. Fewer matches do not establish better chemistry or explain the score comparison.

The seed-0 high-label structure combines a thiol, N-F and densely joined small-ring topology. The seed-2 cage has many unassigned centres and constrained closures; neither lowercase aromatic labels nor permitted sulfur makes these whole graphs geometrically credible.
Very large concatenations and tiny fragments both receive extremely low labels, while reactive and strained-looking compact structures can still receive the higher labels.
missing_features: Less entangled compact realizations of the favorable polar/fluorinated arrangement are not recovered at the Parent labels. The Child supplies cyclopropane-fused and cage alternatives rather than a demonstrated conventional replacement.

Stable nitrogen substitution and credible whole-ring geometry are not consistently present in the leading families. The records do not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore, and the Parent's high labels do not certify its structures.
Stereochemical specification is absent in the substituted cyclopropane and dense cage families; imino/carbonyl tautomeric and conformational identity also remains unassessed.

The Child seed-0 ester/imino/thiol leader reaches 0.4630100785756386; a related dione/methyl version scores 0.3970261111343973, but several local features change together, so this is not an isolated thiol or imine effect. In the seed-1 series, the N-F leader scores 0.382162818465848, its N-Cl relative 0.20570615790249458 and its N-Br relative 0.12523563919780292. That local ordering within questionable chemistry is not a general requirement for N-halogen substitution. transferable_gaps.evidence: Re-observed in n-61c472c961cc against published code Parent n-1744a1494180, on all issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the inherited lock, batch ten and 300 accepted observations per independent session including ten initials. Compact ordinary amide and diaryl-amine leaders coexist with N/O-halogen, N-amino amide, nitroso/nitrite, carbamoyl-chloride and haloaminal alternatives. The linked nitrogen-rich family has 56 acyl-halogen observations versus three Parent observations, whereas a fluorinated polar family has 298 N-halogen observations versus 425 Parent observations. Neither direction is a chemical-quality or component-effect metric. The broader local-environment gap was originally recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, carried by n-62daf219c70a and retained in the published Parent molecular report; those original sources and applicability conditions remain separate.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply conventional functional-group environments while retaining favorable molecular relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer de novo, intact conventional functional-group alternatives preserving relationships supported by current-session feedback. Evaluate attachment context separately from elemental counts or the inherited source-relative sulfur condition. Retain useful amides, amines, thioethers and other ordinary functions where observed feedback supports them. These associations do not justify a universal filter, transfer the source sulfur result, or assign the liability to the encoder, GP, blend or any graph operator.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the complete n-61c472c961cc three-Search-seed panel at batch ten and 300 observations per independent session, recorded structures include connected medium rings, eight/ten/eleven-membered cycles, cyclopropane-fused heterocycles, multiply bridged cages and carbon-allene variants. Comparatively conventional three-aromatic-ring amides and two-aryl amines are counterexamples to uniform geometric deterioration. Ring closure and aromatic string incidences are already high. This continues the geometric gap originating in n-c55c3d520a2c and reported through n-62daf219c70a and published Parent n-1744a1494180; original condition-specific evidence is not pooled into a new effect estimate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid ring generation is not consistently accompanied by credible ring geometry and connected-ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate alternative connections with attention to ring size, bridge connectivity and unsaturated-bond geometry while preserving useful molecular relationships. Keep feasible small, fused, medium and larger rings available; the record supports no blanket ban or numerical ring cap. Molecular graph validity and aromatic labels alone do not establish conformation, synthesis or an endpoint benefit from a geometry intervention.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-61c472c961cc under its complete issued Search panel, inherited lock, batch ten and 300 observations per independent session. Every digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of all recorded optimizer structures finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2115 of 4350 Child observations and 2455 of 4350 published Parent observations, with no explicitly specified centres in either panel. High-label benzylic fluoroamines, fluoroalkoxy groups, substituted small rings and cages are examples; other leaders are achiral by this reading. This re-observes the identity gap originally recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, without changing their original source conditions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generated potentially stereogenic arrangements remain without explicit tetrahedral configuration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or specify stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, handling achiral and configurationally unstable environments separately. Continue to distinguish full isomeric molecular identity from representation views. Protonation and tautomerism need separate assessment: neutral notation does not mean that useful basic centres are absent. These records establish neither a stereochemical score penalty nor a component-specific source of the omission.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-61c472c961cc versus n-1744a1494180 on the complete matched issued Search panel, batch ten and 300 observations per independent session. There are 52 Child optimizer observations with at most three heavy atoms versus 82 Parent observations. Tiny fragments commonly receive the lowest or floor labels; 48- and 51-heavy-atom aromatic concatenations have extremely low labels, and a 120-heavy-atom heterocyclic concatenation falls below its more compact family leader. Conversely, an eleven-membered amide/amine/ether structure and a slightly more cross-linked relative both have useful labels, so growth is not uniformly harmful. This carries forward the conditional context gap originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a in the published Parent report; the lower fragment count is not treated as proof of repair.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful whole-molecule context during fragmentation, growth and reconnection.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use current-session accepted feedback to retain useful combinations of molecular regions when shrinking, expanding or reconnecting de novo graphs. Allow genuine simplification and useful growth. Neither a fixed minimum size nor a universal preference for compactness or aromatic mass follows from these observations, and the chemistry does not attribute context loss to a specific operator.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Re-observed for n-61c472c961cc under the fixed joint recipe, inherited graph/admission rules, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch ten and 300 observations per independent session. Higher-label groups repeatedly vary halogen placement, short chains, carbonyl/imino substituents or closely related ring connections. Distinct seeds do reach different families and ordinary amides/diaryl amines, but larger nitrogen-rich annulations and dense cages do not reproduce some compact Parent high-label arrangements. This is limited plausible alternative coverage, not global scaffold collapse or an ancestry measurement. The original gap provenance remains n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a as retained by n-1744a1494180's published molecular report; their applicability is not rewritten.
transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible independent alternatives to a locally successful scaffold arrangement are not consistently represented among the higher-label molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically independent feasible connectivities that preserve relationships learned from the present accepted observations, and assess their realized labels and chemistry separately. String uniqueness or additional ring closures do not establish useful series coverage. This is task-agnostic generator guidance, not an objective-specific target scaffold, contribution attribution, or a claim that adding diversity will improve endpoints.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
